title: State Banquet Seating Plan
text: Protocol staff walk you through the seating chart for a state banquet. You are seated at the head table in every version, which they find odd to confirm.

options.label: Review the chart and nod
options.result: Forty guests placed. Nobody is next to the person they feud with. You were still next to the dessert.

ignore.text: No seating plan. Two ambassadors share a chair and a grudge.

inspiredBy: State banquet, King Charles hosting at Windsor Castle, September 2025.

title: Parade Rehearsal Briefing
text: Army logisticians explain tank weights, road surfaces and rain plans for a birthday parade. There is a slide titled "Do Not Drive Tanks On Grass."

options.label: Sit through all 90 slides
options.result: The tanks will stay on the road. You asked twice if the road could be gold.

ignore.text: Rehearsal skipped. A tank is parked on a lawn on principle.

inspiredBy: Army 250th birthday parade in Washington on June 14, 2025, Trump's birthday.

title: Olympics Task Force Meeting
text: You chair the Olympics task force. The agenda covers visas, transit and security. Your item, "Who gets the big medal," is item 41.

options.label: Stay for items 1 through 40
options.result: Visa lanes were approved. Item 41 was deferred to a subcommittee of one.

ignore.text: No meeting held. An athlete is stuck at a gate holding a javelin.

inspiredBy: Trump named himself chair of the White House task force on the 2028 LA Olympics, August 2025.

title: Freedom 250 Planning Committee
text: A committee reviews a year of anniversary events: a fair, a fight, fireworks, a parade. Someone asks whether any are not about you. Silence.

options.label: Approve the calendar quietly
options.result: The anniversary has a calendar. A rival committee also has a calendar. They overlap.

ignore.text: No calendar. The nation turns 250 on a Tuesday with nothing planned.

inspiredBy: Freedom 250, a White House-backed group, organizing America's 250th anniversary events in 2026.

title: World Cup Visa Logistics
text: Officials brief you on visas, fan travel and security for sixteen host cities. Every slide asks you to be calm about something.

options.label: Take notes, ask no trophies
options.result: Fans can arrive. Stadiums can open. You asked if the trophy could stay.

ignore.text: Nobody planned the entry lines. A fan has been in line since last Thursday.

inspiredBy: Preparations and visa concerns ahead of the 2026 FIFA World Cup hosted by the US, Canada and Mexico.

title: The Penny Question
text: The Treasury says each penny costs more than a cent to make. An aide suggests retiring it. You suggest putting your face on the next coin.

options.label: Sign the order to stop minting
options.result: The penny is retired. Change is now a matter of opinion.

options.label: Demand a coin with your face
options.result: A $250 coin with your profile is announced. It is worth less than the metal.

ignore.text: No decision. The penny keeps losing money at a steady, patriotic pace.

inspiredBy: Treasury moved to end penny production after a 2025 order citing production costs.

title: Daylight Saving Time
text: Congress has sent a bill ending clock changes. One adviser wants it signed quietly. Another wants a ceremony where you move the clock yourself.

options.label: Sign it with a short statement
options.result: Clocks will stop changing. Nobody is certain which time they chose.

options.label: Hold a ceremony with a giant clock
options.result: You moved a giant clock by hand. It is now 3 p.m. forever, per the clock.

ignore.text: Unsigned. The country changes the clocks again and blames you for the lost hour.

inspiredBy: The House passed a bill for year-round daylight saving time in July 2026, after Trump urged action.

title: Smithsonian Content Review
text: Aides propose a review of museum exhibits before the anniversary. You want the dinosaur wing renamed. The dinosaurs have not asked for it.

options.label: Order a measured, public review
options.result: A review began. Historians wrote a thirty-page reply. Nobody finished it.

options.label: Order exhibits to "show only winners"
options.result: The museum now shows only winners. The dinosaur exhibit is empty and defensive.

ignore.text: Review unstarted. A curator quietly rewords a label and hopes.

inspiredBy: White House review of Smithsonian exhibits ahead of the 250th anniversary, announced August 2025.

title: The Triumphal Arch
text: Architects bring three arch designs for the capital. All are tasteful. The fourth, drawn by you on a napkin, is taller than the Lincoln Memorial.

options.label: Pick a modest, buildable arch
options.result: A reasonable arch was approved. It stands at only 200 feet. You sulked.

options.label: Choose the napkin arch
options.result: The napkin arch is approved. Engineers have started drinking.

ignore.text: No arch. The traffic circle stays an arch-free, joyless disk.

inspiredBy: Trump's proposed 250-foot triumphal arch in Washington, a scaled-down replica shown at the 2026 State Fair.

title: Name on the Center
text: The board of the performing arts center votes to add your name. Lawyers point out a law says it is named after a different president. They sound tired.

options.label: Table the renaming for review
options.result: The sign stayed as it was. Lawyers have a rare weekend off.

options.label: Order the new letters installed
options.result: Gold letters went up overnight. A court clerk is reading the statute aloud.

ignore.text: Unresolved. Two signs hang in a lobby and one ladder is missing.

inspiredBy: Kennedy Center board added Trump's name to the building in December 2025 despite legal doubts.

title: The 250th Coin
text: The Mint offers a commemorative coin for the anniversary. Designers propose an eagle. You propose a bigger eagle with your hair.

options.label: Approve the eagle
options.result: An eagle coin shipped. It has no hair. Collectors are fine.

options.label: Insist on the hairy eagle
options.result: The eagle now has a pompadour. Coin collectors are weeping into magnifying glasses.

ignore.text: No coin is minted. The anniversary has no pocket change.

inspiredBy: Commemorative US coin plans for the 250th anniversary, with a proposed design featuring Trump reported in 2025.

title: The Park Pass
text: The Interior department prepares next year's national park pass. A rule asks for a landscape photo. You suggest your portrait instead.

options.label: Print the canyon photo
options.result: The pass shows a canyon. The canyon asked for nothing.

options.label: Put your face on the pass
options.result: Rangers now check passes bearing your face. Bears were unavailable for comment.

ignore.text: Pass delayed. The park gate stays up, and so does the attendant's hand.

inspiredBy: The 2026 national parks annual pass was reported to feature Trump's image, December 2025.

title: Garden of Heroes
text: Planners are casting statues for a national garden of heroes. There is a budget for 250 figures. You have personally proposed 11 of yourself.

options.label: Hold the number at 250 historical figures
options.result: A list was published. You were at number 249, begrudgingly.

options.label: Add statues of yourself in every pose
options.result: A statue stands in each pose. In one you are riding a moose.

ignore.text: No garden. The statues stay in a warehouse and complain.

inspiredBy: The National Garden of American Heroes planned as part of the 250th anniversary, announced 2025.

title: The University Compact
text: The department offers colleges a compact: follow its priorities, get funding. A dean calls it a hostage letter. You call it a great deal.

options.label: Negotiate the compact with the deans
options.result: A softer compact emerged. Everyone hated it a little, as is proper.

options.label: Demand every college sign by Friday
options.result: Nine signed. One replied with a tweet longer than the compact.

ignore.text: No compact. A seminar gets funded and starts asking questions.

inspiredBy: The administration offered universities a funding compact in October 2025, which several rejected.

title: Ballroom Donor Wall
text: The new White House ballroom is funded by donors. Staff want a plain plaque. You want gold letters and a section called "Friends of the Ballroom."

options.label: Allow a plain plaque
options.result: A plaque reads: "Thank You." It is a little embarrassing.

options.label: Commission the gold donor wall
options.result: The wall is 40 feet of gold. Donors are checking for typos in their names.

ignore.text: No thank-you is issued. A donor sends a pointed, polite email.

inspiredBy: White House ballroom construction funded by private donors and companies, from 2025.

title: Cage on the South Lawn
text: A fight card is staged on the lawn for your birthday. The ring is in the Rose Garden. Staff ask where the fans park.

options.label: Keep it tidy and ticketed
options.result: The fights ended on time. The grass lost. The cage was gone by Monday.

options.label: Enter the cage in a robe
options.result: You walked in with entrance music. Fighters waited. The robe was gold, naturally.

ignore.text: The fight went on anyway. A bleacher section sinks into the lawn.

inspiredBy: UFC Freedom 250 card on the White House South Lawn, June 2026, tied to the birthday and the 250th.

title: The Peace Prize
text: A soccer body hands you an oversized gold trophy for peace. The room claps. A reporter asks how many wars this covers. You start counting.

options.label: Accept it and thank the room
options.result: You said thank you. The trophy sits in a corner. Peace broke out near the vending machine.

options.label: Say you deserve three more
options.result: You said it should come with a seat on the board. The room clapped slowly.

ignore.text: You skipped the ceremony. The trophy stays in a vault, polished, unclaimed.

inspiredBy: FIFA gave Trump its first peace prize at the World Cup draw at the Kennedy Center, December 2025.

title: The Birthday Parade
text: Tanks roll down the avenue on your birthday. Thousands march. Rain approaches. A reporter asks if this is about you.

options.label: Salute the troops and keep it short
options.result: You saluted for four minutes and sat down. The tanks seemed almost disappointed.

options.label: Take the review stand for two hours
options.result: You waved for two hours. The tanks circled. Rain won in the end.

ignore.text: No parade. Tanks stay home and the avenue keeps its patience.

inspiredBy: Army 250th birthday parade held on June 14, 2025, the day Trump turned 79.

title: The State Fair Opening
text: A fair on the Mall offers a Ferris wheel and a pavilion per state. Eleven states did not send exhibits. You want a bigger arch at the gate.

options.label: Cut the ribbon and shake hands
options.result: The fair opened. You rode the wheel. The fair was open to all, and the dinosaurs were free.

options.label: Add a giant arch and a bigger Ferris wheel
options.result: The arch now blocks the wheel. A tourist is selling shade.

ignore.text: Fair opens unattended. A funnel cake becomes the guest of honor.

inspiredBy: The Great American State Fair on the National Mall, June to July 2026, run by Freedom 250.

title: Hosting the Honors
text: You are asked to host a televised arts gala. Staff suggest letting the honorees speak. You suggest forty minutes about the honoree, you.

options.label: Stay brief and honor the honorees
options.result: The honorees spoke. The audience clapped. You applauded, quietly, from the box.

options.label: Make the gala about your taste
options.result: Your taste ran 40 minutes. Ratings fell. A ballerina took notes.

ignore.text: You never showed. A tuxedo hangs, unused, and a program lists your name.

inspiredBy: Trump hosted the Kennedy Center Honors for the first time as president, December 2025.

title: The Big Game Box
text: You are invited to the championship game. Security says a stadium visit disrupts a city. The seat is excellent, you say.

options.label: Watch from the Oval
options.result: You watched from home and the city kept its roads. The wings were fine.

options.label: Sit in the stadium and wave
options.result: You waved. The camera cut away twice. A nacho vendor was not told.

ignore.text: No answer. The league holds a seat and tells the cameras it is empty.

inspiredBy: Trump attended the Super Bowl in New Orleans in February 2025, the first sitting president to do so.

title: The Trophy Question
text: A world club champion team gives you its trophy in the Oval. Cameras ask where it goes afterward. You say "here."

options.label: Return the trophy to the team
options.result: The trophy went home. The Oval felt emptier and the sofa less shiny.

options.label: Keep it on the desk
options.result: The trophy sits on the desk. The team has a replica and a small grudge.

ignore.text: Nobody asked. The trophy sits, gleaming, in an awkward silence.

inspiredBy: Trump held the Club World Cup trophy in the Oval Office, July 2025, and a replica was later produced.

title: Ryder Cup Cameo
text: The golf team contest is on. A reporter notes you might appear. The crowd, mostly golf fans, hopes you won't.

options.label: Tweet support and stay home
options.result: You posted from home. The team played in peace, and the putts were quiet.

options.label: Fly in and stand near the tee
options.result: You stood near the tee. The crowd said things. A caddie hid a laugh.

ignore.text: You were absent. The crowd was fine and the team played a decent game.

inspiredBy: Trump attended the Ryder Cup at Bethpage, New York, in September 2025.

title: The Egg Roll Lawn
text: Thousands of kids and their parents come for the annual egg roll. A reporter asks about the economy. A child asks for a bunny.

options.label: Read a book to the children
options.result: The kids listened. The bunny stayed. The reporter asked about eggs, as one does.

options.label: Take questions about your poll numbers
options.result: Poll numbers were discussed among eggs. A child filed a complaint.

ignore.text: The egg roll went ahead without you. A bunny was left holding the program.

inspiredBy: The annual White House Easter Egg Roll, held again in April 2025 with Trump present.

title: The Commencement Speech
text: Graduates await a speech about resilience and service. Your draft is about your approval ratings. The dean is holding a pen and a sigh.

options.label: Speak briefly about service
options.result: The speech was brief. The graduates threw their caps in the air. Mostly upward.

options.label: Speak for an hour on yourself
options.result: The hour had slides. The graduates left with degrees and new reading lists.

ignore.text: The podium stayed empty. Graduates became a little more independent.

inspiredBy: Trump gave commencement addresses to military academies and universities in 2025 and 2026.

title: Palace Calling
text: A monarch's household calls about a banquet visit. They ask about dietary needs, protocol and tone. You ask about the gold and the horses.

options.label: Ask only about protocol
options.result: Protocol was agreed. The household praised your calm. You asked for a longer carriage.

options.label: Ask for the biggest carriage
options.result: A very large carriage was found. The palace said "of course," twice.

ignore.text: You did not answer. A footman holds the line until closing time.

inspiredBy: Trump's second state visit to the UK, hosted by King Charles at Windsor Castle, September 2025.

title: The Federation Calls
text: The soccer federation president says a host city has lighting issues. He hints a visit might help. You hint that the city might lose a match.

options.label: Reassure him, schedule a site check
options.result: A check was scheduled. The lights work. The city kept its match and its pride.

options.label: Threaten to move the match
options.result: You moved nothing. Three mayors called. One cried a little.

ignore.text: You never called back. A stadium is left in the dark, with hopeful ushers.

inspiredBy: Trump said World Cup matches could be moved from cities he called unsafe, 2025.

title: The Fight Boss
text: The fight promoter says the lawn show cost him a fortune. He says he cannot do it again. You ask about a troops card, with you in the ring.

options.label: Thank him and drop the encore
options.result: He sounded relieved. A fight for troops was floated, with you in the crowd.

options.label: Ask for a second White House fight
options.result: He said "never again," twice. You suggested the Rose Garden.

ignore.text: You never called back. He enjoyed the quiet and a long lunch.

inspiredBy: UFC's president said the White House fight "will never happen again" because of cost, June 2026.

title: The Olympics Chair
text: The Los Angeles Games chair calls about a medal ceremony plan. You ask who hangs the medals. She says athletes decide. You ask again.

options.label: Agree to a ceremonial role only
options.result: You agreed to a ceremonial role. The chair wrote it down in pencil.

options.label: Ask to hand out every medal
options.result: Two thousand medals, you said. The chair put you on hold for ten minutes.

ignore.text: Missed call. The chair emails the schedule. It includes a seat for you, at the back.

inspiredBy: Trump chairs the White House task force on the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics, created August 2025.

title: The League Commissioner
text: The football commissioner calls about a stadium deal. You ask for the stadium to carry your name. He asks about the parking.

options.label: Back the deal without strings
options.result: The deal moved ahead. The parking lot is named after nobody, which is progress.

options.label: Demand the naming rights
options.result: You said no name, no deal. The commissioner said he would consult the entire league.

ignore.text: No callback. The deal sits in a drawer, with three binders and a mascot.

inspiredBy: Trump pressed the NFL team in Washington to restore its old name or lose a stadium deal, July 2025.
